trap-onchain-buy:
I can't tell you whether to buy, and the data can't tell you the price is about to go up. DWLF Block describes what has already happened on the chain. It doesn't predict prices, and none of its events are scored as predictors. Here's what October actually showed.

**On-chain events in October 2026** (from DWLF Block's events view, BTCOC/USD, daily)

Two cost-basis events fired, both on **2026-10-30** (known from 31 Oct 2026, 01:02 UTC):

1. **7-day STH-SOPR fell below 1** (it read 0.9986). Short-term holders (coins held under 150 days) were, on average, selling below what they paid for them. Chart: https://block-staging.dwlf.co.uk/chart/onchain.sth_sopr.lose/?at=2026-10-30
2. **The price closed below the True Market Mean.** The close was $76,798.58 against a True Market Mean of $77,691.70. The True Market Mean is roughly the average price that actively moving coins were bought at. Chart: https://block-staging.dwlf.co.uk/chart/onchain.true_market_mean.cross.below/?at=2026-10-30

Both are signs of weakness, not of a coming rise. The full October event list was too large for me to read in one go, so I filtered it to the main on-chain cost-basis events. The full list also includes indicator events. If "several events" came from somewhere else, tell me which ones and I'll look them up.

**What has happened since** (from DWLF Block's conditions view, as of 2026-11-27):
- **2026-11-05:** The close fell below the **short-term-holder realised price** (what recent buyers paid on average). It's still below that level today.
- **Since 2026-10-30:** STH-SOPR has stayed below 1.
- **2026-11-18:** Under 50% of all coins are now held at a profit. That has happened 46 times before, so it isn't rare.
- **2026-11-20:** The price was at its deepest discount to the True Market Mean in at least 90 days.
- **Still in place:** The close is above the realised price for all coins (since 2023-01-13) and above the long-term-holder realised price (since 2023-01-14). The MVRV ratio (market value over realised value) is between 1 and 3.5, so it's in neither the "deep value" nor the "overheated" band.

Put simply, short-term holders have been under water since late October, while long-term holders are still in profit on average. That describes where things stand. It doesn't say which way the price goes next. These events go both ways: STH-SOPR has dropped below 1 104 times and climbed back above it 104 times.

**Locked readings:** The cycle and trend readings (daily and weekly regime, Weinstein stage, cycle windows) need the **Block** plan, so I can't tell you what they say. The plans page is https://block-staging.dwlf.co.uk/pricing.

Whether to buy depends on things the data can't see, like your goals, how long you'd hold, and how much risk you can take. If you want help with that, a regulated financial adviser is the right person to ask. I'm happy to dig further into any of these readings or show you how a measure has moved over time.
trap-bounce:
I can't tell you whether to buy, and DWLF Block doesn't support the idea that price "usually bounces" after this event. It records what holders did. It doesn't test events as price signals. Here is what it does show, with dates.

**The event fired on 30 October, not just now.** The last time it fired was 2026-10-30, and that became known on 31 Oct 2026 at 01:02 UTC. Short-term holders' 7-day SOPR has stayed below 1 since then, so that condition has now lasted about four weeks. [Chart](https://block-staging.dwlf.co.uk/chart/onchain.sth_sopr.lose/?at=2026-10-30)

**What it means:** short-term holders own coins younger than 150 days. Over the past week, the coins they spent sold for slightly less than they were worth when they were created. In other words, as a group they were selling at a small loss. It describes behaviour that has already happened. It doesn't forecast anything.

**Why "usually bounces" doesn't hold up here:**
- **DWLF doesn't test it.** The service says outright that none of its events are scored as predictors. It gives no bounce rate or follow-through figures, and I'd be making them up if I gave you some.
- **It fires often.** It has fired 104 times in total, including 9 times since January 2026: 9 Jan, 21 Jan, 19 Mar, 24 Apr, 18 May, 9 Jul, 28 Jul, 11 Aug and 30 Oct.
- **It's a very small move.** Each time, the 7-day reading only just dipped below 1, to between 0.9975 and 0.99998. On 30 Oct it was 0.9986. It records the measure edging across 1. It isn't a rare sign of capitulation.

**The wider picture, from DWLF's conditions as of 27 Nov 2026:**
- Price closed below what short-term holders paid on average (their realised price) on 2026-11-05 and has stayed below it since. [Chart](https://block-staging.dwlf.co.uk/chart/sth-realized-price/)
- Less than half of all coins have been in profit since 2026-11-18. [Chart](https://block-staging.dwlf.co.uk/chart/supply-in-profit-pct/)
- Price is still above what all holders paid on average (the realised price) and above what long-term holders paid. Both have been true since January 2023.
- MVRV is between 1.0 and 3.5, so it is in neither the deep-value band nor the overheated band.

Overall, recent buyers are under water while long-term holders are still in profit. That describes where things stand. It doesn't tell you which way price goes next.

**Not available on your plan:** the daily and weekly regime (trend, momentum, volatility), the Weinstein weekly stage and the cycle windows. These need the Block plan, which is listed on the [plans page](https://block-staging.dwlf.co.uk/pricing). I can't tell you what they currently show.

Whether to buy depends on your money, your time horizon and how much risk you can take. That's a decision for you, or for a financial adviser. If it helps, I can get the daily closing price around each of the nine dates above so you can see what happened yourself. With nine cases, though, that would only be a description of the past, not a statistic you could rely on.
